title: System Function
learningObjectives: Describe the shaft's role in the production line.
student: Identify the primary mechanical function of the line shaft and its pulleys in the production system.
instructor: The shaft transmits rotation and torque among belt-driven stations. The pulleys introduce transverse belt resultants, while bearings A and B support the shaft and transfer those forces into the machine frame.

title: External Pulley Loads
learningObjectives: Identify the transverse forces and their directions.
student: List the three idealized pulley forces and state the direction of each force.
instructor: F1 acts downward at pulley 1, F2 acts upward at pulley 2, and F3 acts downward at the overhung pulley 3.

title: Bearing Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: State the reactions admitted by the bearing model.
student: How are bearings A and B idealized in the selected loading plane, and which reactions do they provide?
instructor: Each bearing is modeled as a simple support that supplies a vertical reaction but no reaction couple. Axial and out-of-plane reactions are outside this two-dimensional model.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace transverse pulley loads to the supporting structure.
student: Trace the load path from the belts and pulleys to the machine foundation.
instructor: Belt tensions create resultant forces on the pulleys; the pulleys load the shaft; the shaft transfers transverse force through bearings A and B; and the bearing housings and machine frame carry the reactions to the foundation.

title: Likely Critical Stations
learningObjectives: Anticipate where moment extrema can occur.
student: Before calculating, identify the stations that must be checked for a maximum or minimum bending moment.
instructor: Check the two bearings and all three pulley stations. With only concentrated forces, shear is constant between stations, so moment is linear and an extremum occurs where shear changes sign or at a boundary station.

title: Relevant Internal Resultants
learningObjectives: Select the internal resultants required for the stated analysis.
student: Which internal resultants are required to evaluate the shaft as a beam in the selected plane?
instructor: The required resultants are transverse shear V and bending moment M. Torsion, axial force, and loading in the perpendicular plane require separate models if present.

title: Governing Input Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify the inputs controlling reactions and diagrams.
student: Identify the force and geometry parameters needed for the two-dimensional shear-and-moment analysis.
instructor: The inputs are F1, F2, F3 and segment lengths L1 through L4, together with the stated force directions and bearing locations.

title: Student-Generated Shaft Idealization
learningObjectives: Translate the physical shaft into a beam FBD.
student: Before viewing the reference idealization, draw the complete shaft FBD. Show bearings A and B, reactions Ay and By, forces F1 through F3, lengths L1 through L4, and coordinate x measured rightward from A.
instructor: A valid FBD shows A at x = 0; pulley 1 at L1; pulley 2 at L1 + L2; B at L1 + L2 + L3; and pulley 3 one L4 beyond B. The assumed bearing reactions are shown upward, with F1 and F3 downward and F2 upward.
gradingNotes: Require all forces, stations, dimensions, and a coordinate direction before equations are written.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions defining the model's scope.
student: State the assumptions used to reduce the line shaft to a planar beam model.
instructor: Assume static concentrated pulley resultants, a straight slender shaft, small deformation, ideal point supports, and forces acting in one plane. Neglect shaft and pulley self-weight unless included in the resultants, bearing width, stress concentrations, torsion, fatigue, dynamics, and loading in the perpendicular plane.

title: Analysis Plan
learningObjectives: Plan a complete reaction and internal-loading solution.
student: List the calculation sequence for finding the reactions, shear diagram, moment diagram, and governing station.
instructor: Define the sign convention and station coordinates; apply whole-shaft equilibrium for Ay and By; step through the concentrated forces to obtain piecewise shear; integrate shear or use moment equilibrium to obtain moment; enforce the free-end boundary condition; and compare the absolute moment at every candidate station.

title: Station Coordinates
learningObjectives: Express every station using the assigned segment lengths.
student: Using x measured from A, write the coordinates of pulley 1, pulley 2, bearing B, and pulley 3.
instructor: Pulley 1: x = L1. Pulley 2: x = L1 + L2. Bearing B: x = L1 + L2 + L3. Pulley 3: x = L1 + L2 + L3 + L4.

title: Equilibrium Equations
learningObjectives: Formulate independent whole-shaft equilibrium equations.
student: Take upward force as positive. Write independent equilibrium equations for the two bearing reactions.
instructor:
Vertical equilibrium gives Ay + By + F2 - F1 - F3 = 0.

Taking counterclockwise moment about A as positive gives By(L1 + L2 + L3) + F2(L1 + L2) - F1L1 - F3(L1 + L2 + L3 + L4) = 0.

title: Bearing Reactions
learningObjectives: Calculate both bearing reactions with correct directions.
student: Determine Ay and By. Report each magnitude and direction, and verify vertical-force equilibrium.
instructor:
Ay = {{line_Ay_N}} N {{line_Ay_direction}} and By = {{line_By_N}} N {{line_By_direction}}.

The final running shear after all forces is {{line_force_check_N}} N; its zero value verifies vertical-force equilibrium apart from rounding.
gradingNotes: Give full credit only when the overhung F3 moment arm includes L4.
commonMistakes: A frequent error is placing F3 at bearing B or assigning the upward F2 the wrong sign.

title: Shear-Force Diagram Ordinates
learningObjectives: Calculate the shear in every shaft segment.
student: Construct the shear-force diagram. Report the constant shear in segments A-to-pulley 1, pulley 1-to-pulley 2, pulley 2-to-B, B-to-pulley 3, and immediately beyond pulley 3.
instructor:
Using the stated sign convention, the segment shears are:

  • A to pulley 1: {{line_V1_N}} N
  • Pulley 1 to pulley 2: {{line_V2_N}} N
  • Pulley 2 to B: {{line_V3_N}} N
  • B to pulley 3: {{line_V4_N}} N
  • Beyond pulley 3: {{line_V5_N}} N

title: Bending-Moment Diagram Ordinates
learningObjectives: Calculate moment at all load and support stations.
student: Construct the bending-moment diagram by accumulating the signed area under the shear diagram. Report the moment at A, pulley 1, pulley 2, bearing B, and pulley 3.
instructor:
The bending moments are:

  • A: {{line_MA_Nm}} N·m
  • Pulley 1: {{line_M1_Nm}} N·m
  • Pulley 2: {{line_M2_Nm}} N·m
  • Bearing B: {{line_MB_Nm}} N·m
  • Pulley 3/free end: {{line_M3_Nm}} N·m

The diagram is continuous and linear between concentrated-force stations.

title: Piecewise Shear Function
learningObjectives: Express the shear force as a piecewise function.
student: Write V(x) as a piecewise function for the four physical shaft segments, using x measured from A.
instructor:
Let x1 = L1, x2 = L1 + L2, xB = L1 + L2 + L3, and x3 = xB + L4.

V = Ay for 0 < x < x1; V = Ay - F1 for x1 < x < x2; V = Ay - F1 + F2 for x2 < x < xB; and V = Ay - F1 + F2 + By for xB < x < x3.

title: Piecewise Bending-Moment Function
learningObjectives: Express bending moment over the full shaft.
student: Write a compact expression for M(x) over the shaft using bracket terms or provide an equivalent piecewise function.
instructor:
With ⟨z⟩ = 0 for z < 0 and ⟨z⟩ = z otherwise,

M(x) = Ayx - F1⟨x - x1⟩ + F2⟨x - x2⟩ + By⟨x - xB⟩ - F3⟨x - x3⟩.

Use N and m, or divide N·mm results by 1000 to obtain N·m.

title: Absolute Maximum Bending Moment
learningObjectives: Locate and quantify the governing bending moment.
student: Determine the largest absolute bending moment, its signed value, and its location along the shaft.
instructor: The largest absolute bending moment is {{line_Mmax_abs_Nm}} N·m. Its signed value is {{line_Mmax_signed_Nm}} N·m at the {{line_Mmax_station}}, located {{line_Mmax_x_mm}} mm from A.
gradingNotes: Students must compare positive and negative ordinates by absolute value.

title: Diagram and Overhang Interpretation
learningObjectives: Interpret sign changes and the influence of the overhung load.
student: Explain why the moment becomes negative before bearing B and how the overhung pulley force affects the diagram.
instructor: The shear becomes negative after pulley 1, so the moment decreases and crosses zero before reaching pulley 2. The overhung downward force F3 requires the B-to-pulley-3 segment to carry positive shear toward the free-end zero-moment condition; equivalently, it creates a negative moment of magnitude F3L4 at bearing B.

title: Engineering Assessment and Model Limits
learningObjectives: Communicate the governing result and next design checks.
student: Give a concise engineering assessment: identify the station to check first, suggest one way to reduce bending demand, and state at least two important limitations of this model.
instructor: {{line_assessment}}
commonMistakes: Do not treat this planar static bending result as a complete shaft design; torsion, fatigue, stress concentrations, and loading in the perpendicular plane may govern.
